name: assert_that
title: Assert that certain conditions are true.

origin.description: assert_that is a replacement for stopifnot with an informative error message.

arguments.text: Unnamed expressions that describe the conditions. Separate them by commas rather than combining them with &&.

arguments.name: env
arguments.text: The environment in which to evaluate the assertions.

arguments.name: msg
arguments.text: A custom error message if one of the conditions is false.

origin.details: Returns TRUE when every assertion is TRUE. Otherwise it stops with class assertError. An assertion must be one logical value; a non-logical result, a missing value, or any other length is an error from check_result rather than a caught assertion failure. The manual's dontrun block is not part of example(); this page prints one success and one caught failure.
origin.value: TRUE, invisibly, or an error of class assertError.
origin.example:
x <- 1
print(assert_that(is.numeric(x)))
tryCatch(assert_that(length(x) == 3), error = function(e) cat(conditionMessage(e), "\n", sep = ""))

translation.description: assert_that is a replacement for stopifnot with an informative error message.

arguments.name: assertions
arguments.text: R expressions as strings. Separate them as extra arguments rather than combining them with &&.

arguments.name: env
arguments.text: A dict of names. When omitted, names come from the caller's locals.

arguments.name: msg
arguments.text: A custom error message if one of the conditions is false.

translation.details: Returns True when every assertion is true. Otherwise it raises AssertThatError. An assertion must be one logical value; a non-logical result, a missing value, or any other length is a ValueError rather than AssertThatError. Expressions are strings.
translation.example:
from assertthat import AssertThatError, assert_that

x = 1
print(assert_that("is.numeric(x)"))
try:
    assert_that("length(x) == 3")
except AssertThatError as error:
    print(error)
